messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: streaming tail latency p99 spike detected for /v1/stream/generate in us-west-2. SLO: p99 < 800ms, current p99 ~ 1.6s. Alerting on-call. Pager: eng-oncall.
oncall-bot: auto-investigation attached: logs, recent deploys, kernel/build metadata.
nina: ack, I'm on it. pulling up console -> p95 jumped from 120ms -> 450ms, p99 from 720ms -> 1.6s around 12:04 UTC. Streaming stalls visible on trace spans: decode_kv_write / kv_pagefault.
sandeep: saw the deploy at 12:02 UTC — we rolled a new runtime image with updated compile flags and TRT8 kernels. I added a new compile flag to enable flash-attn fused path: CFLAGS+=-DREDWOOD_USE_FLASHATTN.
jules: got it. Also note we merged a small change in the compile pipeline that toggles the fast-kernel linker (compilepath v3.2.1). Could be interacting with TRT/flash kernels.
nina: copying relevant logs:
```
grep -A2 -E "decode.*latency" /var/log/servers/stream-*-decode.log | tail -n 20
2026-02-18T12:03:05Z [info] decode latency p99=1600ms node=gw-12 kernel=trt8-2026-02-18 build_flags="-DREDWOOD_USE_FLASHATTN -O3"
2026-02-18T12:03:35Z [warn] streaming stall: kv-pagefault idx=0x3a2a pages=48
```
sandeep: that matches what I pushed. I can immediately flip a runtime flag to disable the fused flash-attn path for models using the new kernel.
jules: verification idea: route a small percentage (5-10%) to the non-flash variant first, confirm p99 drops, then scale rollout. We have a runtime knob: models->variant-routing in the console.
mike: infra note — if we route away from the new kernel we'll increase CPU/other kernel pressure on older nodes; autoscale has some slack but keep an eye on queue depth.
ops-bot: created issue RW-INC-3247, linked to this thread, priority P1, assigned to eng-runtime and eng-sre.
nina: performing canary routing now to 10% -> non-flash variant. command: 
```
redwood route update --model text-gen-003 --variant nonflash --weight 10 --region us-west-2
```
(just ran)
ops-bot: route update accepted, rollout id rlt-20260218-01.
nina: monitoring metrics... p99 dropped from 1.6s -> 980ms after 10% traffic diverted. p95 steady.
sandeep: I'll prepare a hotpatch to remove the -DREDWOOD_USE_FLASHATTN compile flag and cut a new kernel build. That should restore behavior without routing changes. ETA for build + deploy ~ 40-50m.
jules: as interim mitigation we should expand routing to 50% and set an automatic fallback for model calls that exceed 1s decode to the non-flash variant. Add a short-circuit in the serving proxy.
tara: SRE ops accepted. I'll stand by for rollback if the build takes longer. Also need customer impact assessment: which customers hit the p99 SLO? cs-rep can you pull list?
cs-rep: pulling from alerts -> Top impacted tenants: beta-corp, opsify, two smaller PLG orgs. Notified CS for beta-corp (they're on a high-throughput feed).
nina: applying escalation steps:
- increase route to 50%
- enable per-request fallback threshold (decode_timeout=1s)
- start kernel hotpatch build
- track p95/p99 and stream stall counts

Applying route change now:
```
redwood route update --model text-gen-003 --variant nonflash --weight 50 --region us-west-2
```
ops-bot: route update accepted, rollout id rlt-20260218-02.
nina: enabling fallback rule in proxy config: 
```
proxyctl set --service stream-proxy --fallback nonflash --threshold 1s
```
ops-bot: proxy config updated.
nina: immediate signs: p99 down to 520ms, streaming stall traces dropping. Good signal.
sandeep: build status: kicked off kernel build job #build-889, linking against trt8-2026-02-01 kernels (no flash-attn). If that passes e2e we'll deploy to canary nodes.
jules: capturing temporary mitigation steps in RW-INC-3247 runbook. Also adding a note to avoid pushing compile flags without perf/regression gating.
mike: infra: I'll pre-warm canary nodes for the new build to speed rollout.
30m later
ops-bot: build-889 succeeded, smoke e2e green.
sandeep: deploying hotpatch to canary pool now. deploy command: 
```
infractl deploy --image redwood-runtime:hotpatch-build-889 --pool canary-usw2
```
ops-bot: canary deploy started.
nina: monitoring canary -> p99 stable ~ 180-220ms. No regressions observed. Rolling to prod in waves.
1h later
ops-bot: rollout complete to prod pool.
nina: final metrics: p95 ~ 130ms, p99 ~ 210ms, streaming stall count back to baseline. SLOs restored.
tara: summarizing customer impact: beta-corp experienced elevated p99 for ~25 minutes before routing mitigation, then partial improvement during rollout; total exposure ~55 minutes. CS notified.
cs-rep: beta-corp support ticket updated with incident summary and ETA for root-change postmortem.
jules: next steps (postmortem actions):
- Add automated pre-merge perf check for compile flags touching kernel/flash paths
- Add canary policy for compiler flag flips (must ship to canary pool only for 1h before prod)
- Improve tracing to correlate compile/build ids with decode spans
- Document fallback knob: REDWOOD_NO_FLASHATTN and runtime routing playbook

nina: handing off to tara for overnight watch and postmortem writeup. RW-INC-3247 assigned to eng-runtime + eng-sre.
tara: taking handoff :white_check_mark: I'll own the postmortem and next-step tracking. If any regressions surface ping me directly.
nina: thanks everyone, good coordination. :thumbsup:
__note: This Slack thread records a single incident coordination exchange; messages are a continuous string with per-message speaker prefixes per agents.md rules.
